prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active form that made possible incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: I keep the single-part B027 prize with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, and my configuration is unchanged from round 1. After reading the full exchange, the case still rests on the science, not on the six identical opening ranks. Holst's incretin and gut-hormone physiology, Drucker's work on proglucagon-derived peptides and receptor biology, and the identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide form a connected discovery arc. It has been confirmed independently for decades and now has outcome-trial evidence in diabetes, obesity, and cardiovascular and renal disease. Timing is not an issue. The round-1 exchange sharpened one thing for me: the citation should be explicit that the discovery of the hormone's physiology and active form is what is rewarded, and that this made the therapies possible, so the prize does not read as a prize for a drug.
statement.case_against: Attribution is still the weak point and round 1 did not remove it. The cap leaves out Knudsen, whose long-acting analogue design produced the drugs patients use. Mojsov's priority for the active peptide is disputed, and Habener, who is outside the credited names, may have a comparable claim. I cannot resolve either point from the supplied material. Naming Mojsov is a judgment that identifying the active form belongs to the discovery chain, and I accept that this is the least secure of the three names. A single-part prize also leaves out a strong second achievement such as B014, B036 or B039, but I do not think that is a reason to dilute a three-person GLP-1 part that already uses the full cap.

responses.point: Sandberg moved from Knudsen to Mojsov in round 1, but said that if the citation names therapy it must say so explicitly so that omitting Knudsen is not read as dismissing drug development. She also asked why I rank B036 above B006 in discovery terms.
responses.response: Your qualification is the right one and my citation follows it. It says the discoveries made incretin-based treatment possible, which acknowledges the therapeutic consequence without crediting the analogue design to the named laureates. I think that is honest, and I would resist widening it further. On your question about B036 and B006: I ranked B006 third at opening because the mechanism is a genuine conceptual advance in innate sensing, but it has no approved therapy and the credit is spread over five names with a priority question between them. For B036 the discovery claim is that, in rheumatoid synovium, TNF sits at the top of a cytokine cascade, and that blocking this single node reverses disease in patients. That was not an expected result and it opened the whole biologic era in autoimmunity. I accept that this is closer to a translational discovery than to a mechanism discovery, which is why I list it as an alternative and not a competing first choice.

responses.point: El Manira called anti-TNF a therapeutic proof of concept built on known cytokine biology that overlaps with IL-6 blockade, and asked what I think the discovery contribution was beyond the clinical trials.
responses.response: My answer is that Feldmann and Maini's contribution was the demonstration, first in human synovial cell cultures and then in patients, that one cytokine is rate-limiting for the production of the others and for tissue damage. Before that, the field did not expect that blocking a single mediator in a polygenic disease would work. I agree that antibody engineering and the original TNF biology are outside the credited pair, and that IL-6 blockade is a related achievement that a committee would have to treat explicitly. Your point also moves my view in one respect: those unresolved boundaries are a good reason not to put B036 in this year's configuration, and I have kept it as an alternative only. I do not rank it ahead of GLP-1.

responses.point: Linnarsson asked whether the citation should reward discovery only or also acknowledge drug development, and said Mojsov's slot is the least certain and needs a close look at the documentary record on Mojsov and Habener.
responses.response: I agree on the framing, and I agree that this slot is the least certain one. On the discovery-versus-development rule, I said in round 1 that I did not want it applied mechanically, and I still think the committee should decide that principle openly. Here I come down on the discovery side, because Holst, Drucker and Mojsov together define what the hormone is, what it does and which form is active. Knudsen's work built on that definition. I would not state the trio as uncontested. If the documentary record on the active peptide were shown to favour another contributor, I would reopen the third name, but I would not move to Knudsen as a response to that uncertainty alone.

responses.point: Svenningsson, the chair, said he would not put TNF ahead of the unfolded protein response on originality but could support it if the committee judged clinical benefit decisive, and asked whether TNF and IL-6 are a single achievement.
responses.response: I do not think TNF and IL-6 are a single achievement. They are separate targets with separate discovery histories, though they are part of the same story of cytokine blockade, and that is the difficulty in drawing a clean citation around B036. I accept your ordering on scientific originality: B014 is more original as a concept. My reason for listing B036 and not B014 as the lead alternative is that, if a second part were required, I would pick a part where patient benefit has been shown over many years. That is a judgment about what the prize is for, not a claim that B036 is the better science. Because you point out that a GLP-1 part with three names leaves no room for a second part under the cap, this is academic for this year's configuration.

uncertainties: Whether the documentary record on the active GLP-1 peptide, including Habener's claim, supports Mojsov in the third place. I cannot verify it from the supplied material.
Whether the committee should state openly that the citation rewards discovery and not analogue design, and whether that leaves the prize looking disconnected from the drugs.
If a two-part prize were wanted, which second part is best among B036, B039 and B014, given the unresolved credit boundaries (TNF and IL-6, Eshhar, and the Walter and Mori attribution).
statement.conflict_note: No conflict requires recusal. B036 (TNF blockade) is close to my field of rheumatology and autoimmunity, but I have no documented personal or institutional tie to Feldmann or Maini, and I draw none from topic area alone. I have no documented connection to any B027 candidate. This is unchanged from round 1.
